changes.current_line: Billing that helps you grow revenue.
changes.change: For product and engineering leaders replacing homegrown billing, lead with roadmap time instead of revenue: 'Stop billing being a tax on the roadmap. Price changes, trials and proration in minutes, not a quarter of engineering work.' Use the demo moment as the proof, since the champion called it 'a quarter of roadmap in five minutes.'
changes.why: The champion rejected the revenue-growth framing outright ('we're not trying to grow revenue with billing, we're trying to stop it being a tax on the roadmap'), and the moment that landed was the pricing-change demo, which he described in roadmap time.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For finance approvers (CFO) on billing replacements, offer to build payback in the customer's own numbers rather than pointing to our study: 'We'll build your payback case with you, from what your current billing costs you today: engineering time per pricing change, billing errors, and subscriptions lost to failed cards.' Offer it as a working session the champion can take to finance.
changes.why: When the champion asked 'do you have something that shows payback?', he got the general ROI deck with the study. He had already said he 'can't get this past Diane without a number that's ours', and that number was never built.

changes.change: For inbound deals where the alternative is doing nothing and there is no deadline, add a cost-of-status-quo message aimed at finance's fire test: 'What keeping your homegrown billing costs you every quarter', backed by a fill-in figure so the problem reads as urgent spend, not a 'nice to have'.
changes.why: The competitor was doing nothing. Finance saw the project as a nice to have under a rule of 'if it isn't on fire, it isn't funded', and nothing in our messaging put a cost on the status quo.

changes.change: For prospects migrating off homegrown billing, pair the migration claims (no re-collection of cards, staged moves, working around renewal-season blackouts) with a peer reference: a named customer who moved off homegrown billing and will take a call.
changes.why: On migration the rep said 'We had a doc for that. He wanted to talk to someone who'd done it.', so a written claim alone did not answer the buyer's risk question.
